china_race_dynamics.text: AI is already changing how we work, live, and learn. We need a plan to protect our national security and workforce. I want the United States to continue to be a leader in AI race but develop this technology in a responsible manner that protects people and communities. To do so, we must get a bipartisan conversation started and work faster to address the challenges and opportunities presented by AI.

deepseek.reason: The speaker discusses general AI leadership and responsible development without mentioning China or competition with China.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The generic 'AI race' reference does not identify China as the competitor, leaving the target relevance uncertain.

astra.reason: The speaker supports responsible US leadership in AI but does not identify China as the competitor.
astra.confidence_reason: Neither the statement nor its context connects the general AI race to China.

china_race_dynamics.text: The reality is if we want to grow and develop some of these emerging technologies like AI and others, we will need more data storage and data centers is a part of that. What we don't need is data centers to be steamrolling communities and being put in places that don't want them. [...] People talk about the issue with China, but honestly people who are seeing their utility bills double and triple don't care about the race against China. We're gonna lose that race, because 70% of Americans now don't want data centers in their community.

deepseek.reason: The speaker dismisses the China race as not addressing voters' utility-bill concerns and warns it is being lost due to local data-center opposition.
deepseek.confidence_reason: The statement clearly criticizes race framing but does not explicitly say competition should be deprioritized.

astra.reason: He warns that community opposition undermines the race with China without clearly endorsing or rejecting competition as a policy priority.
astra.confidence_reason: The dismissal of the race is attributed to residents, while his own remarks leave its priority ambiguous.
